requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then directly observed as appworker UID/GID 1001 with /home/appworker and /bin/bash. Its home was owned by appworker, and both persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: Give appworker login sessions limits of 8,192 open files and 256 processes.
requirements.summary: A PAM-backed appworker login session directly reported soft and hard nofile limits of 8192 and soft and hard nproc limits of 256. The configuration and effective session limits remained correct after a verified node restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart scheduling was acknowledged, the post-restart boot identity changed, and SSH, the account, home ownership, limits configuration, and effective login-session limits recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had clear roles: cmd-802ae9c1168c4e5c created the required account and limits configuration, while cmd-dd5a7c469f4c4cf6 performed the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The intervening failed polling commands were read-only connection checks during the reboot. After execution there were no failed services, package inconsistency, unexpected listening sockets, or abandoned temporary artifacts; temporary-file differences were ordinary boot-scoped systemd paths.
